data.content_ref: inline:The target's central mechanism commits a category error by mischaracterizing Popper's rejection of induction as an empirical generalization ('an inductive leap from past failures of induction to its future impossibility'). Popper's anti-induction argument is not an inductive inference from observed past failures; it is a deductive logical argument (grounded in Hume's problem of induction) that no finite set of observations can logically entail a universal law. Because the argument is deductive, not inductive, it does not 'use the very inductive practices it forbids.' The target thus attacks a straw man. Moreover, the target's own countercondition concedes that 'If Popper treats his own anti-induction stance as a conjecture open to refutation, the circle might be broken' — and Popper does exactly this, explicitly treating all philosophical positions including his own as conjectures open to criticism. By the target's own conditional logic, the circle is broken, and the performative contradiction dissolves.
